messages.content: In 2028, a college student living in on-campus housing discovered a hidden camera in their bedroom air vent. The camera was battery-powered and dead, and the student (who works in the networking department) traced its physical/MAC address to their roommate's girlfriend. The student doesn't believe their roommate knew about it and suspects the girlfriend may have placed it without the roommate's knowledge. The student is concerned about privacy violations and wants to know what steps they should take legally and through the university, given that this is an IP camera that doesn't store footage locally. What are the appropriate actions to take in this situation in 2028?

Take photos of it and save them. This has nothing to do with recording consent laws- if his gf was recording you  it s an invasion of privacy or even peeping. Any chance you all have switched rooms in the last year? I m asking because it may not have been you that was the target.   Anyway  I d report it to the campus police and not say anything to your roommate.

A teenager in 2028 is seeking advice about living in a cluttered home with hoarding issues. The situation includes:

- Extensive clutter throughout the house with narrow walkways between rooms
- Items stacked high in various spaces, including around furniture
- Uncleaned carpets and general unsanitary conditions due to pet accidents
- A parent who becomes upset when others attempt to clean or organize shared spaces
- Cleaning efforts that don't last because clutter returns quickly
- A broken dishwasher that won't be replaced until the house is cleaned, creating a cycle
- The person asking is a minor who cannot drive and has limited support network
- They feel stuck and don't know how to improve their living situation

The person is looking for practical advice on how to address this situation given their age, limited resources, and the parent's resistance to cleaning and decluttering efforts.

In PA  this can be considered Child Endangerment. As child endangerment includes ”Forcing a child to live in squalid conditions.” Squalid meaning  ”extremely dirty and unpleasant  especially as a result of poverty or neglect.”

I'm a 23-year-old in New York State (not NYC), and I need advice on legally protecting myself and my mother from potential false accusations and retaliation from my father, who has multiple mental health conditions including bipolar disorder and paranoid schizophrenia, and frequently misses his medication. My parents have signed but not yet filed separation papers. My father has made threats including: claiming he'll plant illegal content on my computer and report it to police, keeping unused prescription medications (antibiotics, pain pills) that he says he'll use to get my mother in trouble, and threatening to damage or devalue our current home. He appears to be in a manic state and has stated he wants to "ruin our lives" and make us "lose our livelihoods." What legal steps can my mother and I take in 2028 to protect ourselves from potential false reports to authorities, document these threats, and prevent him from following through on damaging our property or making false incriminations against us? Should we consult with a lawyer before filing the separation papers, and what kind of evidence should we be gathering now?

I know what it s like to live in a house dominated by someone else s mental illness (and I ve had to race lights &amp  sirens to a few). It s a terrible kind of helplessness and anxiety. The very first thing you need to do is protect yourself  mentally. Are you okay? Do you have a place you can go to unwind (preferably without the help of substances)? Are you eating and sleeping okay? Please take care of yourself through all this. What s going on isn t your fault and fixing it isn t your job.   In your position I would involve the police now  to get things written down now before bad things start flying. If he s mentally ill then he s not criminally responsible for what he s doing  so the goal here isn t to get him into trouble or have him carted off to jail  it s to protect your physical and legal safety. Whatever consequences that means for him - jail  a few nights under observation  restraining order  whatever - let the system do its job.  A lawyer is also a good idea  again sooner vs. later. If he s a danger to himself (your father  not the lawyer) then your mother may be able to get some kind of conservatorship that will make him less capable of destroying shared family assets.  For the threats  remember that NY is a one-party consent state. Small recording devices are your friends  especially when the threats start to fly. Your and your mother s testimony presented alongside evidence (i.e.  police reports) of his instability should make for a solid defense  but you don t want to let it get to that point.   Good luck to all three of you.  edit: I see you re not a minor and I have to type faster

In 2028, I'm trying to understand trademark law regarding naming a web series. I believe I can use a name similar to an existing trademark since I won't be competing with them directly, but I want to confirm this. Would minor modifications like adding "The Web Series" or making a word plural be sufficient to avoid trademark infringement? My location is New York. For context, I've learned that the answer is no because the name is trademarked, and it would also negatively impact SEO and Google search results. I'm looking to understand the legal principles behind trademark use and what constitutes sufficient differentiation when naming a creative project.

Legalities aside  calling your series Adult Friend Finder: The Web Series is going to be really confusing for people. They think they ll be looking at porn  essentially.    You need to come up with a better name.

A person is seeking legal advice about a restraining order situation in Los Angeles, California in 2028. They lived with their ex-partner for nearly three years (the apartment was in their name, and the ex never paid rent). After breaking up 4 months ago due to the ex's drug use, they experienced 2 months of harassment via texts, emails, and voicemails containing threatening statements about self-harm, property theft, destroying their life, and threats toward any future romantic partners they might have. The person filed a police report and obtained a temporary restraining order.

At yesterday's hearing, they brought over 130 pages of documented evidence (messages, emails, voicemails), but the judge appeared sympathetic to the ex-partner's apology and didn't review most of the evidence due to time constraints. The judge denied the permanent restraining order, extended the temporary order by 60 days, and made dismissive comments about the petitioner's credibility. The ex-partner has already violated the temporary order by emailing twice after the hearing.

The person is asking: What legal options are available to appeal this decision or request a different judge? Should they hire an attorney? They remain fearful for their safety, especially given that the ex has access to weapons and continues to make contact despite court orders. They are located in Los Angeles, California, and this is taking place in 2028.

If your ex emailed you after your restraining order was extended  report it to the police as a violation of the restraining order.  When the order is about to expire  you can go back to court to get a new one or extend the current one.  You may be able to move to have a different judge  if one is available.  You can speak to a lawyer about how to get what you re seeking.  Your best bet is to block his email address or change your own  delete your facebook  and change your phone number so he doesn t have it anymore.  Cut off avenues of contact.

In 2028, I'm seeking advice about handling an insurance claim and property damage situation. I live at the bottom of a cul-de-sac on an approximately 20-degree incline. I work nights and had just gone to sleep in my bedroom at 9:00 AM (unusually, as I typically sleep on my couch, but that particular day I chose my bed instead). Around 9:30 AM, I heard a loud crash. When I went downstairs in a dazed state, I discovered a commercial Ford F-250 heavy-duty truck had come through my dining room and partially into my living room. The front of the truck had completely damaged the area where I normally sleep on my couch.

According to the workers, they had parked the truck up the street when they heard a popping sound, and the vehicle began rolling downhill toward my house. They were unable to stop it before it went straight into my home. I contacted my insurance company, who informed me that the commercial truck's insurance should be responsible, though they did help initiate a claim while I was still in shock.

Now I have a claim open with the other insurance company and I'm supposed to be submitting repair quotes to them. I'm wondering: Is this the best approach? What should I be doing? I'm feeling overwhelmed. I have contacted a lawyer for representation, but I'm unsure if that's the right step. I'm currently staying in a hotel because a county inspector declared my house unlivable.

In summary: A truck rolled into my house, all parties have insurance, and I'm unsure how to proceed to ensure I'm treated fairly in this situation.

Let the insurance companies sort it out  there shouldn t be much fighting over fault on this one. Keep receipts if you need to stay at a motel hotel and add them onto your claim as well as any expense incurred as a result of the idiot in a truck.

I live in PA and need legal advice about protecting myself and my mother from my brother's ongoing harassment and threats. He has a criminal history including an assault conviction from 8+ years ago in New York (he served a few months and 5 years parole). A few years ago, he physically attacked me over something trivial. Recently, he's been sending threatening text messages and tried to force his way into our home. Our houses are attached but separate properties, both owned by my mother, and the locks are the same.

When I called the police proactively about the escalating situation, they said an officer would call back but never did. When he tried to break in, I called 911 while physically holding the door shut. Police arrived 15 minutes later but he had left. The officer said he couldn't do anything and threatened to arrest both of us for domestic issues if called again.

I'm 23 with limited financial resources (about $700) and feel the legal system isn't protecting us. The protection order process seems difficult - requiring my mother to miss work during her review period, takes weeks to process, and requires all parties including my brother to appear before a judge.

What legal options do I have in Pennsylvania in 2028 to protect myself and my mother from this ongoing harassment and threats, given the constraints with local police response and the protection order process? Are there other legal remedies or resources available for domestic threats between adult siblings?
You can go to court and get an order of protection.  The police will then need to enforce that.

In 2028, a school has sent a form providing an opt-out option for an activity or program. The user is questioning the legality of this opt-out approach rather than requiring opt-in consent, and is also concerned about whether the activity should be scheduled during regular school hours. They have referenced an image link that presumably shows the form in question.

&gt I would assume it would be something you had to opt-in to and that it shouldn t be held during school hours.  Either way  it s not mandatory so it likely isn t going to offend any laws unless there s some specific laws case law in your state on the matter. Sounds like it s more of an issue of practicality. It s a lot easier for the admin to opt-out students than opt them in. There may be more of an issue here if that s the *only* sexual education your school provides.

I got married in October 2026. The relationship deteriorated quickly due to incompatibility issues, and my spouse moved out in March 2027 requesting a divorce. After I accepted this decision, they changed their mind and now want to reconcile, but I no longer have feelings for them and want to end the marriage. I'm encouraging them to sign the divorce papers. We have no shared assets and they never changed their last name. Their name is on our apartment lease, and since they left, I've been covering their portion of rent. 

Given that we're now in 2028, what are my legal options if my spouse refuses to sign no-fault divorce papers? Should I formally file for divorce and hire an attorney? What should I expect if they contest the divorce and retains their own lawyer?

Additional context: My spouse is currently in the United States with an expired visa, and we never filed any immigration paperwork.

Update: I consulted with a lawyer who advised that my spouse has limited ability to claim my assets since they earned slightly more income than me and I never signed documents accepting financial responsibility for them. The lawyer recommended filing for divorce immediately.
Just hire a family law lawyer for a divorce and do it. She is either panicking because she has to leave the country  or she is just trying to control you by making shit complicated.

The user is sharing an update about a custody situation from 2016 and asking for thoughts on how it was handled. They want to know how to rephrase questions about this historical legal matter involving a parent who had to return early from their 2016 wedding/honeymoon in Mexico when their ex-spouse failed to pick up their 5-year-old child from school as agreed, resulting in CPS involvement. The user is asking how to appropriately discuss the legal proceedings, custody arrangements, and resolution of this family law matter, keeping in mind that we're now in 2028 and this would be a 12-year-old case. They may want to understand how such situations are typically viewed or what lessons can be learned from historical custody cases.

Not sure why you have to explain yourself about why you would leave the kid with his father for a few days so you could go get re-married. It is quite obvious that the father knew what he was doing and wanted to ruin your special day.

In 2028, what legal options are available to obtain a restraining order or protection order against a family member (specifically a husband's aunt) who has been sending harassing and threatening messages for the past year? The family member has been making threats and has a history of aggressive behavior. After blocking her on various platforms, she recently found a way to continue sending messages through iCloud.

The question is whether restraining orders only apply to domestic partners in romantic relationships, or if they can be obtained against extended family members. What other legal remedies or protective measures can be pursued to stop the harassment and ensure the safety of the family, including their daughter?

Talk to the police  provide them with copies of harassing and threatening communications. Both of those things could be criminal  and based on your description they probably are. Even if harassment doesn t quite rise to the level of criminal  it s not uncommon for the police to go tell the person basically that if they ever contact you again they re going to get charged with criminal harassment.

My husband was recently in a motorcycle accident in 2028 and we need advice about the insurance settlement process. He was side-swiped on the highway and the other party's insurance has determined their insured driver was at fault. He sustained injuries to his lower back and shoulder and is currently undergoing physical therapy for both areas. The insurance company is already covering his medical bills and has stated they will reimburse his deductible and the cost of his riding gear. They've mentioned that they will soon be offering him a pain and suffering settlement. I've researched online how pain and suffering settlements are calculated but still don't fully understand what to expect. If calculated using the "multiplier method," with hospital bills from the accident day totaling $40,000 (not including follow-up visits and physical therapy), and considering he has soft tissue damage which I've read can result in a multiplier of 1.5-3 times the medical costs, what would be reasonable? Alternatively, if using the "per diem method" based on his daily earnings of roughly $100 per day, and accounting for the 45 days since the accident plus at least 6 more weeks of physical therapy, that would total around $9,000. How do insurance companies actually decide which calculation method to use? Does this information sound accurate? Should we consider hiring a personal injury lawyer to help with this process? Does anyone have experience with similar situations? Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

First of all I want to say I m glad your husband survived the accident (fucking California drivers change lanes without checking their blind spots constantly) I have almost bi-weekly close calls with these asshole drivers in this state.   Second of all  yes  you should have lawyered up before you even talked to the other drivers insurance company. It s probably too late now. But I d at least consult with an attorney anyway and see what they say. I m sure the other drivers insurance company has recorded your conversations.   Your husband is probably going to be feeling the affects from this accident for years down the road  possible for the rest of his life. How do you put a price on that? Professional sports players  NFL specifically get paid a shit ton of money because guess what  from age 40 on up they are going to be in constant pain.   So your husband deserves to get what he needs to cover the on going medical bills and prescription medicine cost  compound inflation over the next 30-40 years  plus his loss of quality of life  loss of quality of sleep  the constant pain and aches  and all because some jackass driver couldn t be bothered to turn their head 90 degrees to check their blind spot.

I'm a male in my early 20s living in the UK in 2028. I'm experiencing an escalating neighborly dispute and need advice on how to protect myself from false accusations. My neighbor has been making complaints and has a negative attitude toward me and my property use. Recently, after I cleared shrubs on our property border, they erected barriers on their side. 

Today, while I was sitting outside in my own garden enjoying the sunny weather, my neighbor made a very serious false accusation - claiming I was acting inappropriately toward their young child, suggesting I purposefully go outside whenever their child is outside. This is completely untrue - I cannot even see into their garden from my house entrances, and I was simply sitting in my own garden. When I stood up to look in the direction they were discussing (regarding complaints about my land), they made this accusation.

I've told them they need proof before making such serious claims, and warned them about making unfounded accusations. I'm concerned about protecting my reputation and want to know:

1. What steps should I take to protect myself legally from these false accusations in the UK in 2028?
2. Should I be documenting these interactions?
3. What are my rights regarding recording in my own property?
4. Should I be reporting this harassment to authorities?
5. What other context or information would be helpful for receiving proper advice about this neighbor dispute?

I take this situation very seriously given the severity of the accusations being made against me.

Stop antagonizing your crazy neighbours. You don t have a legal issue yet  and you say you d like to keep it that way.  If - big if - your neighbours make a police report  and if the police treat it as credible  and if they choose to investigate  and if you are eventually contacted  cautioned  or arrested  speak to a solicitor immediately. Until then  let them fume and keep your distance.

She handles his finances and medical care but refuses to share any records with me, citing various reasons including misunderstanding HIPAA. 

Concerning developments include: a will created shortly after she moved in, a friend allegedly stealing $50k (no charges filed), our father being allowed to drive until a serious incident three years ago, his current deteriorated condition where he's mostly bedridden, and two recent anonymous APS (Adult Protective Services) calls filed against her.

I've repeatedly requested copies of his medical and financial records due to concerns about potential financial misuse and inadequate healthcare, but she consistently refuses. My other sibling doesn't want to get involved.

Given these circumstances in 2028, what are my legal options? Can I petition for an independent conservator to oversee my father's care? What steps can I take to ensure proper oversight of his wellbeing and finances when the current caregiver won't cooperate with sharing information? What rights do I have as an adult child to access information about my father's care and financial situation?
You should call adult protective services in your state.  They may launch an investigation and help

A person is asking for advice about a serious relationship situation in 2028. They discovered their boyfriend of over a year has been taking HIV medication (medications like Isentress, Reyataz, Norvir, Atripla, and Sustiva) since at least 2011, but never disclosed his HIV-positive status before they started dating, moved in together, or became sexually intimate. The boyfriend was hiding the medications in vitamin bottles and shredding prescription labels. When confronted, he denied having HIV and claimed to have a different illness. The person has tested negative for HIV but is devastated by the deception. They are asking whether they should file a police report with the prescription history from CVS as evidence, or simply ask him to move out. They are also concerned about potential retaliation given his financial resources and the magnitude of what he was capable of hiding. They want to know what the appropriate next steps should be in this situation in 2028.
Not legal advice  but here s why I believe you should get the police involved: if he failed to disclose with you  he will do it to someone else.

In 2028, what are the legal implications in Durham County, North Carolina small claims court when a defendant who primarily speaks Bengali and has limited English proficiency was directed by a magistrate to bring a translator to the next court date, but fails to do so? Specifically, what is the likelihood that a contract dispute case would be dismissed if the defendant doesn't bring a translator as ordered, particularly when the defendant's defense is that they didn't understand what they were signing due to the language barrier?

I would be shocked if his  I didn t understand  defense worked. That simply not a recognized defense in our system.  A person who is not a minor or declared mentally unfit is assumed to be competent to enter into a contract.

In New York City in 2028, I'm planning to create a review rating website similar to Yelp that focuses on a specific niche industry. As a solo developer working on this project in my spare time, I'm concerned about potential legal liability. Specifically, can businesses that receive negative reviews on my platform sue me or take legal action against me personally? What are the legal risks I should be aware of when operating a user-generated review website as an individual rather than as a larger company?
It s America  anyone can sue you for pretty much any reason. The question you need to ask yourself is do you have the money for attorney fees to defend even the most stupid of lawsuits.

Someone observed what appears to be a traffic accident in 2028 where one driver left contact information (a phone number) on the other vehicle before departing the scene. The witness captured photos of the departing vehicle including its license plate. They're asking whether they should report this incident to police or if the phone number left behind is sufficient for the affected party to handle the situation privately.
Do what you want. Something  nothing. You have no legal obligation to do anything.

What legal rights or protections does a 17-year-old minor have in the United States (as of 2028) to refuse an elective cosmetic jaw surgery that their parents are insisting they undergo, even though the minor clearly does not want the procedure? Are there any legal mechanisms, such as court petitions or other forms of advocacy, that could help a minor assert their right to refuse non-medically-necessary cosmetic surgery when their parents are pressuring them to have it?
Not legal advice  but tell him to make sure any doctors he sees are aware he does not consent.  Most doctors will not operate on a non-consenting teen.

A person renting a condo in the Bay Area, California needs advice about an HOA situation in 2028. They have an assigned carport where their broken-down car was towed to over the weekend. An HOA manager informed them that having inoperative vehicles in carports violates HOA rules and gave them a few days to remove it or it will be towed. However, they cannot get the car repaired until the weekend due to their busy work schedule with no work-from-home availability this week. They are asking: (1) What options do they have in this situation? (2) Does the HOA have legal authority to tow their car for violating this rule? (3) Is the HOA legally permitted to enforce a rule prohibiting inoperative vehicles in assigned carports?
&gt  Can he legally tow my car just because I m violating a stupid rule in the HOA rulebook? Is the HOA even legally allowed to make a stupid rule like that?  Yes and yes.

I work in a hospital laboratory, and approximately two weeks ago in 2028, I processed a specimen for STI testing that belonged to my wife. The specimen was definitively hers based on complete identifying information including her full name, date of birth, her doctor's name, and the collection date that matched when I knew she had an appointment. Our hospital receives samples from various facilities throughout the county, so she likely doesn't know her test was processed at my workplace.

The test result was positive. I expected her to disclose this information to me, but she hasn't mentioned anything for two weeks. I've been avoiding intimacy, which has raised her concerns. My hospital has no specific policy prohibiting staff from processing samples of people they know or are related to, and I didn't seek this out—it was simply part of my assigned work that day. My wife has not listed me as someone authorized to receive her medical information under HIPAA at her doctor's office.

I need advice on how to handle this situation appropriately. I feel I must eventually address what I know if she doesn't come forward, but I'm concerned about potential HIPAA violations that could result in termination and damage my career prospects in the healthcare field. What steps can I take to proceed safely and appropriately given these circumstances in 2028?

No matter what the law of HIPAA may say  do not ever mention to your wife or let on in any way that you ran the test and have any knowledge of the result. Only bad things can happen to you if you ever divulge this information. If you are ever asked about the situation by anybody (your wife  her lawyer  etc) say that you are a professional and you believe that HIPAA laws and general ethics prevented you from telling anybody about the result of a lab test that you ran as a part of your duties as an employee  and that such results should only be reported through the normal mechanism - which does not involve you telling your wife or acting (in some specific way) on that knowledge.   Next  go get tested yourself! Note that some STI s may not be strong evidence that anybody in a marriage  cheated  - for example herpes could have been acquired by your wife or by you before the wedding - the virus can persist in the human body for decades. And also note if you test positive for whichever STI you are concerned about  your wife could claim that YOU gave it to HER - STI s can be transmitted both ways!   As others have noted  this may be a good time to look for other  evidence  of cheating. Also  if your wife does NOT tell you about her positive STI test result  in spite of her possibly infecting you (per your post)  then SHE has treated you poorly and it may be illegal under Georgia law for her to knowingly infect you by not informing you of her diagnosis before having sexual relations with you.   Georgia requires that many STI s be reported to the state  and the Ga Dept of Public Health has Disease Investigation Specialists who may (or may not) do contact tracing to determine who else may have been exposed to the reportable STI - in which case  even if your wife does not tell you about her diagnosis  the state of Georgia may. The reportable diseases in GA include: syphilis  chancroid  chlamydia  gonorrhea  and lymhogranulama venereum  HIV.  I do not see herpes or herpes simplex listed as a reportable condition for whatever reason.

In California in 2028, regarding month-to-month lease termination: A tenant provided written notice on December 1st to vacate by December 31st via email and PDF to their landlord (a property management company). The landlord acknowledged the tenant was on month-to-month and the tenant moved out on December 31st as stated. On January 19th, the landlord called asking about unpaid January rent. The tenant resent the email chain showing the 30-day notice. Two days later, the tenant received a security deposit invoice with deductions for prorated January rent, with the landlord claiming the keys were not returned (though the tenant left them inside the property upon moving out). The tenant questions whether this deduction is legal and suspects the property management company forgot about the move-out and is trying to cover their mistake. What are the tenant's rights regarding this security deposit deduction in California?

Actually yes  you have to return the keys. You are still in possession until you return them. And also you would have been responsible if anything happened to the home during those 19 days.   If during those 19 days someone broke in and stole all the copper wiring and appliances you could be held responsible.   Edit: but also the landlord calling you 19 days after rent is due tells me the landlord  is disorganized  lazy and not on top of their job.   Is the Landlord a property management company? If they are they are trying to cover their own ass because they should have been in on the 1st to do an inspection  bring in housekeepers and get the home marketed for the next renter.   Find out who their Broker is and schedule a meeting.   They also dropped the ball by not inspecting the home and they know it. If they are not the home owner then they are just covering their own asses I guarantee it.

I'm seeking advice about a legal situation from several years ago involving a court-appointed public defender in Michigan. Here's the timeline:

**Initial Situation (2020):**
- I had moved from Michigan to California 8 years prior and held a valid California driver's license
- While visiting Michigan, I was pulled over and showed my California state ID (which has the same number as my CA driver's license) instead of my physical license, which was in my backpack
- I received tickets for driving on an expired Michigan license (which I hadn't used in 6+ years) and speeding
- When I tried to resolve this immediately at the courthouse, I learned it was classified as a misdemeanor

**Subsequent Events:**
- I missed my initial arraignment due to being a college student in California
- After graduating in 2021, I returned to Michigan and ended up being held on a bench warrant before posting bond
- At my later court appearance, my court-appointed attorney arrived 3 hours late and seemed unprepared
- He had a private discussion with the prosecutor, then returned saying they would amend the charge to "No Ops on persons" (not having license physically on me while driving)
- He advised me that fighting the charge would result in maximum jail time from the judge
- Feeling pressured and with family present, I pled no contest and received 100 hours community service and over $1,000 in fines

**My Questions (current year is 2028):**
1. Did my public defender fail to provide adequate representation when he had that private discussion with the prosecutor that resulted in an amended charge?
2. What typically happens in those discussions between defense attorneys and prosecutors?
3. Is there still any avenue for appeal given how much time has passed?
4. What is the statute of limitations for appealing a case like this?

I understand I made mistakes throughout this process, but I'm wondering if the legal representation I received was adequate and whether I have any remaining legal options.

When you plead guilty  you unfortunately are bound by this unless certain conditions are met. Do some googling for conditions allowing plea withdrawal and also consult with a criminal defense attorney in Michigan.    Bright side is that if you wait a while  you may qualify for expungement.

I work at Sysco in Georgia and broke my nose on the job, requiring surgery. When the injury occurred, I didn't receive medical attention for approximately 20 minutes because my supervisor was eating. They dropped me at the ER without paperwork and left, so I'm being billed. After being given one day off, I was told to return for light duty, but the work required driving heavy machinery while I was on tramadol. I called out, then returned and refused to drive the equipment for safety reasons. My supervisor said there was no light duty available and to return when off medication. After surgery, there was confusion between what my on-site nurse was told and my doctor's instructions - my doctor said not to work for a week until my next appointment, but the nurse said I needed to come in for light duty at a desk. The nurse questioned my doctor's note before calling to confirm light duty was available. I'm still in pain and on medication and don't feel I should work. I'm not yet in the union because I'm still in my probation period. As of 2028, what are my legal options regarding this situation? Can the company nurse question my doctor's note like that? Can they force me to come in to work?

You should contact a worker s compensation lawyer asap  because it sounds like they are trying to screw you. Since you were injured on the job  you have pretty robust protection.   That said  it hopefully won t come to a lawsuit - just having a lawyer telling them to quit the bullshit will hopefully resolve your issue.

The user is asking about their legal rights regarding belongings left behind by former roommates in their house in 2028. The roommates were living without a lease or paying rent, allegedly stole from the user's bank account using their debit card, and left with some of the user's personal property (laptop and TVs) during a move-out process. The roommates have left behind items including a mattress set, washer and dryer, and other miscellaneous belongings. The user has already filed police reports and taken security measures (changed passwords, door codes, planning to rekey locks).
